<hr />

## 1. Summary

1. **Background and rationale**: Woody encroachment increases the cover and height of bushes and trees in ecosystems whose characteristic condition is open. It can result from land-use abandonment, reduced grazing or haymaking, drainage, climate change and other changes in disturbance regimes. The indicator describes structural change in naturally open areas, semi-natural land and wetlands.

2. **Methods**: Canopy height is predicted from ordinary aerial orthophotos with Meta's High Resolution Canopy Height model. The 1 m workflow uses overlapping image chips, quality screening and a versioned calibration of the model output. Object-level canopy height is normalised between X~100~ (good-condition reference height) and X~0~ (complete deterioration represented by mature-forest height). Object values are aggregated with area weights. Intensively mapped calcareous open ground (GRUK; T2-C-7/T2-C-8) is calibrated to its estimated share in the ANO open-lowland frame. Uncertainty is estimated with a spatial cluster bootstrap.

3. **Interpretation**: An indicator value of 1 signifies open vegetation structure consistent with the good-condition reference. Values decreasing toward zero indicate increasing woody vegetation height relative to the stratum-specific interval between X~100~ and X~0~. The metric describes vegetation structure, not all components of ecological condition.

4. **Results and development needs**: The provisional national V1.2 estimate is **0.9170** (95% uncertainty interval 0.8910--0.9392). The estimate is coverage-limited and combines imagery from several acquisition years. The frozen X~100~ package used for V1.2 and the generation provenance for the X~0~ forest table must be committed before the indicator can be considered independently reproducible and operational. Reference choices should subsequently be reviewed by NiN main type.

## 2. About the underlying data

The workflow combines aerial imagery, mapped ecosystem objects, reference polygons, regional strata and bioclimatic zones. The current V1.2 delivery includes ANO, ASO and GRUK objects. The result table retains the raw height statistic, calibrated canopy height, reference levels, eligibility fields, spatial cluster and aggregation weights for every object.

### 2.1 Spatial and temporal resolution and extent

The candidate workflow uses 1 m orthophotos in ETRS89 / UTM zone 33N (EPSG:25833). Source tiles cover 2 x 2 km and contain 2,000 x 2,000 pixels. Inference uses overlapping 256 x 256 pixel windows with 64-pixel overlap. The reporting label is 2024, and V1.2 excludes observations after 2024. The available imagery is a spatial mosaic of acquisition years rather than a simultaneous national survey.

### 2.2 Sampling design

ANO and ASO provide probability-sample information, whereas GRUK polygons are mapped much more intensively around the Oslofjord. Direct area weighting would therefore allow GRUK to dominate the national estimate. V1.2 defines GRUK as T2-C-7/T2-C-8 and calibrates its national contribution to the proportion of these units among 1,081 points in the approved ANO open-lowland frame. One such point was observed nationally.

### 2.3 Original units

Canopy height, X~100~, X~60~ and X~0~ are expressed in metres. Object area is expressed in square metres. The final indicator is dimensionless and bounded between 0 and 1.

### 2.4 Instructions for citing, using and accessing data

The model code is based on Meta's High Resolution Canopy Height repository at fixed revision `84971392fb3a017e53d19e28ee0409d0de5d5d61`. Aerial imagery originates from Norway in Images. Small reference and configuration files are stored with the indicator workflow. Orthophotos, model checkpoints and full delivery products are maintained outside GitHub because of licensing and file size.

### 2.5 Additional comments about the dataset

The earlier nationwide 2 m result was a technical pipeline test. It is not the current indicator estimate because predicted heights at 2 m were strongly compressed toward zero. The 1 m candidate uses a separately versioned height calibration.

## 3. Indicator properties

### 3.1 Ecosystem Condition Typology Class (ECT)

Woody encroachment is assigned to B3, functional state characteristics, because it describes a change in vegetation structure and ecosystem functioning relative to characteristically open conditions.

### 3.1.1 Other condition typologies

The indicator contributes to Norwegian ecosystem-condition assessments and is methodologically related to the LiDAR-based indicator NO_GJEN_001.

### 3.2 Ecosystem condition characteristic

Open vegetation structure.

### 3.3 Collinearities with other indicators

Vegetation height can covary with vegetation productivity metrics such as NDVI. In wetlands, woody encroachment may also covary with drainage indicators. These relationships should be considered when indicators are combined in an ecosystem-condition assessment.

### 3.4 Impact factors

Important impact factors include abandonment or reduced intensity of grazing and haymaking, drainage, planting or removal of trees, altered fire and disturbance regimes, nitrogen deposition, invasive species and climate-driven shifts in the forest line and shrub growth.

### 3.5 Spatial aggregation

Canopy height is scaled and transformed at object level. V1.2 aggregates the transformed values using calibrated area weights. Within the GRUK and other-open-lowland domains, relative area weights are retained. The national combination is the ANO-estimated GRUK share times the GRUK-domain mean plus the complementary share times the other-open-lowland mean. Values are truncated to the interval 0--1. Regional estimates currently use observed regional GRUK shares and are provisional where the ANO frame contains no GRUK point.

## 4. Reference condition and levels

### 4.1 Reference condition

The reference condition is a minimally disturbed state with native species composition and an open vegetation structure characteristic of the ecosystem. In naturally open ecosystems this means that drainage, climate change, alien species and other pressures have not caused net woody encroachment. In semi-natural ecosystems it assumes continued management, such as grazing or haymaking, sufficient to maintain open conditions.

### 4.2 Reference levels

X~100~ represents good condition and is based on canopy-height estimates from good-condition NiN reference polygons, stratified by ecosystem group, region and bioclimatic zone. Each population object inherits the reference value for its stratum.

X~0~ represents complete deterioration by woody encroachment. The implemented 1 m workflow reads X~0~ from `reference_forest_1m_v0_4.csv`. The same mature-forest height is used for all ecosystem groups within a region-zone stratum. In the strata represented in V1.2, X~0~ ranges from 3.844 to 11.743 m. The current production code does not implement a separate 0.8 m X~0~ override for naturally open ecosystems.

For canopy height $h$, define

$$z=\operatorname{clamp}\left(\frac{h-X_{100}}{X_0-X_{100}},0,1\right).$$

The condition value is

$$I(h)=\operatorname{clamp}\left[1-1.0068\left(1-\exp(-5z^{2.5})\right),0,1\right].$$

The implementation rejects reference strata for which $X_0 \leq X_{100}$.

X~60~ is not independently estimated. Solving $I(h)=0.60$ gives

$$X_{60}=X_{100}+0.400116533\,(X_0-X_{100}).$$

Thus the implemented X~60~ lies almost exactly 40% of the interval from X~100~ to X~0~. Defining an ecological X~60~ independently would constitute a method change.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Frozen-reference contract

The repository candidate X~0~ table reproduces all 3,759 frozen V1.2 object references exactly. The file `reference_good_1m_v0_4.csv` currently in the repository is not the frozen X~100~ table used for V1.2: none of the object-level X~100~ values are exact matches, although all delivery strata are present, and the largest absolute difference is 0.609 m. The candidate table must not replace the frozen delivery values. The generating X~100~ package must be recovered and versioned.
:::

An X~0~ of 0.8 m cannot be introduced independently of X~100~: 1,000 of 3,113 naturally open V1.2 objects already have X~100~ greater than or equal to 0.8 m. The three reference levels should therefore be reviewed jointly, preferably by NiN main type as well as region and bioclimatic zone.

#### 4.2.1 Spatial resolution and validity

Reference levels vary by ecosystem group, one of five reporting regions and bioclimatic zone. They are regional-stratum references rather than local measurements. Object-level values are retained for transparency, but inference and interpretation are intended at national and regional scales.

## 5. Uncertainties

### 5.1 General uncertainties

The canopy-height model is less precise for very low vegetation and shaded areas. Differences in acquisition year, season, camera system and georectification can affect predictions. Reference polygons and mapped GRUK objects are spatially biased. The ecological meaning of mature forest as X~0~ may differ among semi-natural grasslands, coastal heath, boreal heath, semi-natural strand meadows and naturally open systems. The current reference provenance gap adds version uncertainty that is not represented by the numerical interval.

### 5.2 Reported uncertainties

The reported 95% intervals describe uncertainty around the aggregated point estimate caused by spatial sampling. They are calculated from 20,000 Bayesian spatial cluster-bootstrap replicates over 10 x 10 km clusters. The ANO GRUK share is re-estimated within every replicate. These intervals do not incorporate model-prediction error, alternative reference definitions, imagery-year uncertainty or classification error.

## 7. Import and prepare datasets

### 7.1 Aerial imagery and model configuration

The production configuration is stored in `config_x100_1m_v0_4.yml`. It fixes the imagery resolution, coordinate reference system, model revision, checkpoints, image-normalisation quantiles, output scaling and calibration parameters.

```{r import-config}
#| eval: false
library(yaml)
cfg <- yaml::read_yaml(here::here(
  "indicators", "NO_GJEN_002", "config_x100_1m_v0_4.yml"
))
```

### 7.2 Reference tables and frozen delivery values

The candidate lookup tables can be imported as follows. The frozen V1.2 object table remains authoritative for reproducing the delivered result.

```{r import-reference}
#| eval: false
reference_dir <- here::here(
  "indicators", "NO_GJEN_002", "data", "x100_reference_v0_4"
)
good_reference <- read.csv(file.path(reference_dir, "reference_good_1m_v0_4.csv"))
forest_reference <- read.csv(file.path(reference_dir, "reference_forest_1m_v0_4.csv"))
```

## 8. Spatial units

The basic calculation units are mapped ecosystem objects or probability-sample objects. Reference strata are intersections of ecosystem group, reporting region and bioclimatic zone. Uncertainty clusters are 10 x 10 km grid cells. Final reporting units are Norway and five regions: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern Norway.

## 9. Analyses

### 9.1 Canopy-height inference and calibration

Inference uses the fixed model revision and checkpoints recorded in the configuration. Model predictions outside 0--10 m are excluded from the polygon height statistic, and at least 80% of covered weight must be retained. The coverage-weighted mean is transformed by a piecewise-linear 1 m calibration with a knot at 1 m, lower slope 3.7522924593 and upper slope 0.7369730202.

### 9.2 Object-level condition

The production implementation is contained in `R/calculate_indicator_x100_v0_4.R`. The essential transformation is shown below.

```{r condition-function}
#| eval: false
scale_encroachment <- function(height, X100, X0) {
  denominator <- X0 - X100
  invalid <- !is.finite(height) | !is.finite(X100) |
    !is.finite(X0) | denominator <= 0
  z <- pmin(pmax((height - X100) / denominator, 0), 1)
  condition <- 1 - 100.68 * (1 - exp(-5 * z^2.5)) / 100
  condition[invalid] <- NA_real_
  pmin(pmax(condition, 0), 1)
}
```

### 9.3 GRUK calibration and uncertainty

Let $p$ be the T2-C-7/T2-C-8 share in the ANO open-lowland frame, $\bar I_G$ the area-weighted GRUK-domain mean and $\bar I_O$ the area-weighted mean for the remaining open-lowland domain. The calibrated estimate is

$$\hat I=p\bar I_G+(1-p)\bar I_O.$$

The same estimator is applied in every spatial bootstrap replicate after resampling 10 x 10 km clusters and re-estimating $p$.

### 9.4 Reproducibility checks

The synthetic contract test validates the 1 m calibration and end-to-end calculation. It passes together with the numerical Pilot85 contract: 0.96271791 for 591 eligible polygons. A separate audit reproduces every frozen V1.2 object indicator after production rounding and verifies the X~0~/X~100~ version relationship described in Section 4.2.

## 10. Results

| Reporting area | V1.1G direct area weight | V1.2 GRUK calibrated | 95% interval |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| Norway | 0.9670 | **0.9170** | 0.8910--0.9392 |
| Northern Norway | 0.9905 | **0.9313** | 0.8904--0.9630 |
| Central Norway | 0.9495 | **0.8963** | 0.8425--0.9402 |
| Eastern Norway | 0.9542 | **0.9259** | 0.8685--0.9636 |
| Western Norway | 0.8704 | **0.9612** | 0.9237--0.9829 |
| Southern Norway | 0.9216 | **0.7795** | 0.6295--0.9037 |

The national ANO frame contains one T2-C-7/T2-C-8 point among 1,081 open-lowland points, corresponding to 0.0925%. Approximate national source weights after calibration are 89.21% ANO, 10.70% ASO and 0.0925% GRUK. Four regions contain no observed GRUK point in the ANO frame, while Southern Norway contains one among 114 points; regional estimates are therefore provisional.
